THINGS TO NOTE BEFORE CONDUCTING THE FOOD OFFERING RITUAL (MENGSHAN FOOD BESTOWAL)

1. LOCATION

This ritual should be performed outdoors in the yard, on the street, or on a veranda/balcony, because wandering spirits and preta souls can more easily assemble and accept food offering and spiritual deliverance in open spaces. (It should not be performed inside living rooms, except for internal repentance rituals for personal karmic creditors).

If you live in an apartment without a private balcony, you can place a small table near an open window or go to a public park/quiet outdoor area.

2. OFFERINGS

Offerings are simple and purely plant-based (vegan):
• Clean, clear water (1 small bowl or cup)
• Cooked rice or uncooked rice grains mixed with sesame seeds (a small bowl)
• A few sweet pastries, biscuits, or candy
• Incense and candles/tea-lights (if fire safety permits)
Important: Never offer meat, alcohol, or animal products.

3. MINDSET AND ATTITUDE

The essence of the Mengshan Food Bestowal is not the physical quantity of food, but boundless compassion (Karuṇā) and the spiritual empowerment of the Mantras and Buddhas' Names. When reciting, maintain sincere reverence, visualizing that through the Buddha's grace, each grain of food and drop of water transforms into oceans of sweet celestial ambrosia (amṛta) that relieve the hunger, thirst, and burnings of all wandering spirits, guiding them to rebirth in Amitābha Buddha's Pure Land.

THE LITURGY OF FOOD BESTOWAL TO HUNGRY SPIRITS (MENGSHAN FOOD OFFERING)

Mantra for Purifying Speech Karma:
Oṃ śucite śucite mahā-śucite śuśucite svāhā. (3 times)

Mantra for Purifying the Three Karmas:
Oṃ svabhāva-śuddhāḥ sarva-dharmāḥ svabhāva-śuddho 'ham. (3 times)

Mantra for Shattering the Hells:
Oṃ karaday svāhā. (3 times)

Mantra for Eradicating Fixed Karma:
Oṃ pra-marda-ni svāhā. (3 times)

Mantra for Purifying the Dharma Realm:
Oṃ raṃ svāhā. (3 times)

INVITATION OF UNSEEN SPIRITS & SINCERE ASPIRATION

(The practitioner kneels with palms joined and recites):
"Today, I, disciple [Name / Dharma Name], prepare this modest, pure vegetarian offering. With utmost sincerity, I respectfully invite all my personal karmic creditors from beginningless lifetimes—whether in human form, ghostly form, or animal form—across the six destinies, whether dwelling within my body or outside, who have ever suffered harm, grievance, or sorrow through my past actions.
I also reverently invite all lonely spirits, wandering souls, and hungry preta ghosts who have no families, no shelter, and no offerings, who wander in cold hunger, and all spirits with karmic affinities in this local area: May you all rely upon the boundless spiritual power of the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha to assemble here and receive our offering of food, drink, and Dharma nectar.
May you receive this modest feast, rely upon the Buddha's compassionate guidance and the sacred sūtras, be freed from all suffering and pain, and swiftly be reborn in the Western Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss to enjoy eternal joy." (1 bow, repeat 3 times)

INCENSE OFFERING TO THE WRATHFUL MAHASATTVA

May the wondrous Dharma and all Bodhisattvas,
Śrāvakas, Pratyekabuddhas, and Holy Sages,
Manifest as luminous clouds of light,
Pervading the realms of the ten directions.
Inspiring all living beings
To bring forth the supreme Bodhi Mind,
Leaving behind all unwholesome karma,
And together perfecting the Unsurpassed Way.
Namo Incense Offering Flaming-Faced Mahāsattva Bodhisattva (Avalokiteśvara). (3 times, 1 bow)

THE EMPOWERMENT MANTRAS

Mantra for Opening the Throat:
Oṃ bu-pū-ti-ri ga-ta-ri ta-thā-ga-tā-ya. (3 times)

Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva's Karma-Eliminating Mantra:
Oṃ ārolik svāhā. (3 times)

Namo Great Compassion Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva. (7 times)

The Wish-Fulfilling Wheel King Dhāraṇī (Cintāmaṇicakra):
Namo Buddhāya • Namo Dharmāya • Namo Saṅghāya •
Namo 'ryāvalokiteśvarāya Bodhisattvāya Mahāsattvāya Mahākāruṇikāya •
Tadyathā: Oṃ cakra-varti cintā-maṇi mahā-padme ruru tiṣṭha jvala ākarṣāya hūṃ phaṭ svāhā. (3 times)

"Reverently bowing to the Great Compassionate Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara: Relying upon the merit of this Dhāraṇī and the boundless empowerment of the Buddhas, may these offerings transform according to the wishes of all spirits assembled here, multiplying infinitely so that all are fully satisfied without lack." (1 bow)

Food-Multiplying Dhāraṇī (Biến Thực Chân Ngôn):
Namo sarva-tathāgatāvalokite oṃ saṃbhāra saṃbhāra hūṃ. (7 times)

Sweet Dew Water Dhāraṇī (Cam Lồ Thủy Chân Ngôn):
Namo surūpāya tathāgatāya tadyathā: oṃ suru suru pra-suru pra-suru svāhā. (3 times)

EXHORTATION TO REBIRTH IN THE PURE LAND

Respected spirits and unseen beings: When the Fundamental Teacher Śākyamuni Buddha was in the world, he taught that past hundreds of thousands of kotis of Buddha-lands to the West, there is a world named Sukhāvatī (Ultimate Bliss), where Amitābha Buddha presently expounds the Dharma.
That world is adorned with seven treasures, filled with jeweled lotus ponds and pure ambrosia. It is completely free from hunger, cold, sickness, deformity, or enmity. Those reborn there attain immeasurable lifespan, progressing irreversibly toward supreme Buddhahood.
Those who wish to be reborn there need only bring forth sincere faith, mindfully recite "Namo Amitābha Buddha", and dedicate their hearts toward rebirth.
Now let us all recite together with single-minded devotion:

PRAISE OF AMITĀBHA BUDDHA

Amitābha Buddha's body is the color of gold,
His splendid marks and brilliant radiance are incomparable.
The white curl between his brows revolves like Mount Sumeru,
His clear blue eyes are vast as the four great oceans.
Within his radiant aura manifest countless transformation Buddhas,
And limitless Bodhisattvas appear within his light.
His forty-eight great vows deliver all living beings,
The nine grades of golden lotuses carry all to liberation.
We take refuge and prostrate to Amitābha Buddha,
In the Western World of Peaceful Sustenance.
We now bring forth the sincere resolve for rebirth,
Beseeching the Compassionate One to receive and guide us.
Namo Western Land of Ultimate Bliss, Great Kindness and Great Compassion Amitābha Buddha.

NAMO AMITĀBHA BUDDHA (NAMO A DI ĐÀ PHẬT)
(Recite 108 times or continuously)

Pure Land Rebirth Dhāraṇī (Wang Sheng Zhou):
Namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya tadyathā: amṛtodbhave amṛtasaṃbhave amṛtavikrānte amṛtavikrāntagāmini gagana kīrtikare svāhā. (3 times)

Mantra for Completing Omissions:
Oṃ huru huru jaya-mukhe svāhā. (7 times)

THE THREE REFUGES

I take refuge in the Buddha, wishing that all sentient beings understand the Great Way profoundly and bring forth the supreme Bodhi Mind.
I take refuge in the Dharma, wishing that all sentient beings penetrate the Treasury of Sūtras and attain wisdom as vast as the ocean.
I take refuge in the Sangha, wishing that all sentient beings lead the great assembly in harmony, without any obstruction.

DEDICATION OF MERIT

May the merit and virtue accrued from this food offering
Eradicate karmic obstacles for all our karmic creditors and wandering spirits.
May all be born together in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss,
Swiftly perfecting Unsurpassed Supreme Enlightenment.
Namo Ever-Abiding Triple Gem of the Ten Directions. (3 times)
